daily_summary.html:
Domestic Politics

The Constitutional Court's ruling on Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's educational qualifications continues to generate significant political fallout. Golkar stated Gibran's fate depends on party leaders, while lawyer Denny Indrayana plans to visit party chairpersons to discuss the Court's decision. All nine Constitutional Court justices were reported to the Judicial Ethics Council for alleged ethical violations in handling the case, and Gibran was reported to police following the ruling.

  • President Prabowo announced that the state will subsidize hajj costs for the 2027 pilgrimage season.
  • KPK Chairman questioned Nusron Wahid's commitment after the minister failed to appear for questioning, saying he "can't manage his time."
  • The KPK received a complaint from PCNU Sekadau regarding alleged money politics at the NU National Congress.
  • DPR members want the Traffic Law bill to penalize parties profiting from overweight trucks.
  • Commission VII selected five candidates for RRI's Supervisory Board for the 2026-2031 term.
  • The Copyright Bill will include provisions covering music royalties and journalistic products.

Foreign Policy & Defence

President Prabowo urged TNI and Polri to boost professionalism amid global risks during a meeting with senior military and police officers. The directive comes as the government announced significant military leadership changes, with Lieutenant General Iwan Setiawan appointed as the new Kostrad commander and Lieutenant General Tri Budi Utomo designated as Deputy Army Chief of Staff.

  • Indonesia joined a global coalition to protect children in the artificial intelligence era.
  • Indonesia proposed global royalty standards to WIPO and urged "safety by design" principles in global AI development.
  • Indonesia urged global action on rising sea levels that threaten island nations.
  • Indonesia and the Netherlands strengthened education and research cooperation.
  • Indonesia seeks stronger US trade ties through a reciprocal trade agreement.

Other

President Prabowo launched a Rp 180 trillion downstreaming project at Weda Bay today, representing a major industrial development initiative. Meanwhile, Coordinating Minister Luhut assured investors that Indonesia's economy "will not collapse" amid market concerns. The government is also considering a moratorium on new nickel smelters due to oversupply conditions.

  • TikTok deactivated 9 million child accounts to comply with Indonesian regulations, while Threads has not yet reported on deactivating accounts of children under 16.
  • Indonesia will cut e-commerce fees by 50 percent for eligible local MSMEs.
  • The government allocated hundreds of trillions of rupiah for transforming community health centers and regional hospitals from 2027-2029.
  • Indonesia plans 14,000 km of new and reactivated railway tracks by 2045.
  • Hotspots in Sumatra surged to 4,845 points, with dangerous haze blanketing Riau province.
